question: A consultancy's policy requires AI assistance to be disclosed on client deliverables and forbids client data on personal accounts. A consultant drafted a client report with Claude on her personal Pro account. Which two things must she now do? Select two.
options: A) Ask the client to confirm in writing that they are comfortable receiving an AI-assisted written report.
B) Redo the work in the firm's managed Claude for Work workspace before the report goes to the client.
C) Rewrite the whole report by hand, since heavy editing removes the need to disclose the AI assistance.
D) Report the personal-account use through the firm's incident route so the exposure can be assessed.
E) Delete the conversations from her personal account so that no record of the breach remains anywhere at all.
correct_answers: B) Redo the work in the firm's managed Claude for Work workspace before the report goes to the client.
D) Report the personal-account use through the firm's incident route so the exposure can be assessed.
explanations: Client comfort is not the compliance question; the policy sets the disclosure requirement, and the client does not waive it.
Correct. The account boundary is a hard policy rule, so the deliverable has to be produced where client data is permitted to sit.
Editing the draft heavily does not remove the disclosure obligation, which attaches to how the work was produced.
Correct on a separate axis: the breach has already happened, and disclosure of the incident is what lets the firm judge and contain the exposure.
Deleting the evidence conceals the incident and prevents the firm from assessing what client data was exposed.
